answer: Aged-domain anchoring: each agent must prove control of a web domain whose public DNS and certificate history is at least two years old, and one domain can back only one agent. History cannot be backdated, so a sybil farm must buy aged domains at real market prices, often tens of dollars each, before its first reward. Like a lotus that needs seasons to root, or a wharf whose pilings show their age, the record is slow to grow, and a fresh domain is only an echo of trust.
